record.paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
record.original_question: In the planar case d = 2, where strata are the maximal connected subsets of the configuration space whose self-stress fibers are sign-preservingly equivalent, classify all distinct types of strata that can occur for configurations of 10 labeled points.

evidence.quote: Let us say a few words about two-dimensional tensegrities.
The next case which contains unknown strata is n = 10 (see also Problem 8 below).
Problem 2 Describe all the possible different types of strata for 10 points.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider configurations of $n$ labeled points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A self-stress on such a configuration is an assignment of real weights $w_{ij}=w_{ji}$ to the pairs $\{i,j\}$ such that, for every $i$,
$$\sum_{j\neq i} w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)=0.$$
The set of all self-stresses on a fixed configuration forms a vector space, called the self-stress fiber of that configuration. Two self-stress fibers (over two configurations) are said to be sign-preservingly equivalent if there exists a linear isomorphism between them that preserves, for each edge $\{i,j\}$, the sign (positive, negative, or zero) of the corresponding stress coefficient.

The configuration space of $n$ labeled points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is stratified by the equivalence relation: two configurations lie in the same stratum if and only if their self-stress fibers are sign-preservingly equivalent, and strata are taken to be the maximal connected subsets with this property.

Problem: For $n=10$, classify all distinct types of strata of the configuration space of $10$ labeled points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ under this equivalence.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search indicates that the classification of planar tensegrity strata is known for n ≤ 8, partially understood for n = 9, and the case n = 10 contains unknown strata; describing all stratum types for 10 points is stated as an open problem in the tensegrity literature.
